AM-S4S-D7.not_flagged_by_the_audit: This clause was found by this lane's own mechanical sweep and adjudication, not by the architecture audit. It is superseded because it is the clause that would otherwise let an implementing lane skip the decisive pre-probe at SECTION_C.
AM-S4S-D7.OLD_verbatim: DERIVED MECHANICALLY, not assumed. The three storage.objects policies call auth.uid(), auth.uid() reads ONLY the request.jwt.claim.sub / request.jwt.claims GUCs, and evidence upload, download and delete work in the product today. If the claims GUC were absent on the Storage API's connection, auth.uid() would be NULL, the helper would receive NULL as user_id, the membership EXISTS would match nothing, and EVERY storage operation would already be denied. It is not. Therefore the Storage API publishes the verified JWT claims onto the connection that evaluates the policy.
AM-S4S-D7.NEW: THE DERIVATION IS VALID ONLY FOR THE SUBJECT CLAIM, AND ONLY DISJUNCTIVELY. MEASURED in this lane at db/baseline/stella_g2_schema.sql lines 486-492, auth.uid() is COALESCE(nullif(current_setting('request.jwt.claim.sub', true), ''), nullif(current_setting('request.jwt.claims', true), '')::jsonb ->> 'sub')::uuid. Because it is a COALESCE over TWO different GUCs, the fact that auth.uid() is non-NULL on the storage connection proves only that AT LEAST ONE of request.jwt.claim.sub or request.jwt.claims is populated. It does not identify WHICH. It therefore does not establish that the request.jwt.claims JSON object is present at all, and even where that object IS present it establishes nothing whatsoever about whether GoTrue includes a session_id member inside it. The corrected statement is: the Storage API publishes the verified SUBJECT identity onto the evaluating connection. Whether it publishes a session_id is UNKNOWN and is NOT derivable from the fact that storage works today.
AM-S4S-D7.the_respect_in_which_it_is_superseded: ONLY the scope of what the derivation proves - narrowed from 'the verified JWT claims' to 'the verified subject identity, by one of two possible GUCs'. The reasoning about fail-closed behaviour and about auth.uid() being the reader is preserved and is correct. No mechanism decision rests on the superseded breadth; M11 already requires deriving session_id server-side from verified claims rather than inferring it, and that requirement is untouched.
AM-S4S-D7.consequence: This is the clause that makes SECTION_C a HARD PRECONDITION rather than a prudent extra check. With the derivation narrowed, the presence of session_id on the storage connection is an open question of fact that S4s cannot proceed without answering.

SECTION_B_MINIMUM_SERVICE_TOPOLOGY.why_Kong_is_not_needed: Two independent reasons, and the first is the load-bearing one. (a) THE PROOF IS STRONGER WITHOUT IT. RI-08 asserts that a subject calling the Supabase Storage API DIRECTLY with its own JWT, bypassing every server route, is still bound by the selected-organization boundary. Targeting storage-api directly makes that bypass literal: the test supplies the real user JWT itself, and no gateway sits in the path to normalize, inject or reject credentials. With a gateway present, a refusal is ambiguous between gateway routing, gateway auth and the storage policy - which is exactly the attribution failure F-S4S-1 already warns about, reintroduced one layer up at the transport. (b) IT IS NOT LOAD-BEARING FOR ANY REQUIRED PROOF. PostgREST may likewise be targeted directly for RI-09. No frozen control in the effective manifest asserts a property OF the gateway, so a topology without one omits nothing any control needs. MEASURED corroboration that the gateway is not the subject under test: the literal 'kong' returns ZERO files across scripts/**, tests/** and supabase/** at 89022a9b - the one part of the original L7 measurement that was both true and relevant.
SECTION_B_MINIMUM_SERVICE_TOPOLOGY.why_the_other_six_are_not_needed: None appears in any required or optional proof of the effective S4s contract. Realtime, imgproxy, Studio/pg_meta, Analytics, inbucket/SMTP and the edge runtime carry no part of the selected-organization storage boundary. MEASURED at supabase/config.toml, the canonical developer stack enables realtime, studio, local_smtp and edge_runtime and would start them - which is one concrete reason the canonical stack is a poor certification substrate as well as a forbidden one: it enlarges the flake and attack surface of the gate for zero proof value.
SECTION_B_MINIMUM_SERVICE_TOPOLOGY.is_this_topology_a_ceiling_or_a_floor: A FLOOR ON THE REQUIRED SET AND A CEILING ON THE JUSTIFIED SET. An implementing lane MUST stand up all four REQUIRED services. It MUST NOT add any of the seven listed services and call the addition necessary for THIS proof. If a future control genuinely needs one of them, that control needs its own authority, not an inference from this section.
SECTION_B_MINIMUM_SERVICE_TOPOLOGY.scope_limit: This section binds TEST TOPOLOGY only. It does not prescribe how the four services are started, in what order, by what tool, on what network driver, or in what file. Those are SECTION_E architectural properties or are deliberately left free.

SECTION_C_F_AUD_2_DECISIVE_PRE_IMPLEMENT.status: BINDING PRE-IMPLEMENTATION REQUIREMENT. This is a HARD GATE ON S4s IMPLEMENTATION, not a test to be written alongside it.
SECTION_C_F_AUD_2_DECISIVE_PRE_IMPLEMENT.requirement: BEFORE any S4s database or application implementation is written, the future disposable real-integration substrate MUST prove that a REAL Supabase Storage API request causes the evaluating PostgreSQL connection to expose current_setting('request.jwt.claims', true)::jsonb ->> 'session_id', or an equivalent exact presence proof of the session identifier on that connection.
SECTION_C_F_AUD_2_DECISIVE_PRE_IMPLEMENT.where_the_probe_must_execute: From inside a helper or policy evaluation that is REACHED BY AN ACTUAL storage-api REQUEST. The observation must be made on the connection the Storage API opened, during a request the Storage API drove. An observation made anywhere else is not this probe.
what_is_NOT_sufficient: Manually executing SET or set_config on request.jwt.claims and then reading it back. This fabricates on one connection exactly the propagation the probe exists to measure - the identical defect v1.0.0 SECTION_7 RULE_1 already forbids, and the lesson the retired PG-2 recorded.
Injecting the GUC from the test harness by any other route, including a connection-level parameter, a session preamble, a pooler setting or a wrapper function.

Proving only auth.uid(), or only the sub claim. AM-S4S-D7 establishes that auth.uid() is a COALESCE over two distinct GUCs and that its non-NULL result identifies neither which GUC was populated nor any other member of the claims object.

Decoding the JWT in Node, or reading session_id off a supabase-js session object, and asserting the value exists. That proves GoTrue MINTS the claim. It proves nothing about whether the Storage API PROPAGATES it to PostgreSQL, which is the only question that matters here.
SECTION_C_F_AUD_2_DECISIVE_PRE_IMPLEMENT.why_this_probe_is_decisive_rather_than_p: The entire S4s mechanism keys the mirror on session_id (M03) and requires the storage policy path to read that session_id off the evaluating connection (M12). If the Storage API does not publish session_id onto that connection, the mechanism as frozen in SECTION_2 cannot be enforced at the storage transport at all - and no amount of implementation effort would discover that any earlier than the first real-integration run, after the database and application surfaces were already written and after the ODS lineage had been spent.
SECTION_C_F_AUD_2_DECISIVE_PRE_IMPLEMENT.outcome_if_session_id_IS_present: S4s implementation proceeds under the effective authority unchanged. The probe becomes a standing positive control - declared as RI-D-P-04 in the companion manifest amendment - and is NOT retired once it has passed, because it measures a managed service's behaviour that can change under upgrade.
SECTION_C_F_AUD_2_DECISIVE_PRE_IMPLEMENT.outcome_if_session_id_is_NOT_present: S4s IMPLEMENTATION MUST STOP. This is a fail-closed stop, not a workaround trigger. AUTHORITY RE-ADJUDICATION is required before any further S4s work, and specifically the SECTION_2 mechanism decisions M03, M11 and M12 would have to be reopened by an authorized lane. No implementing lane may, on its own authority, substitute an alternative carrier for session_id, fall back to auth.uid() alone, route the value through the application, or narrow the control to whatever the transport happens to supply.
SECTION_C_F_AUD_2_DECISIVE_PRE_IMPLEMENT.no_prejudgement: This amendment takes NO position on which outcome the probe will produce. It is a genuine open question of fact about a managed service's propagation behaviour. The whole point of making it a hard gate is that it be answered by MEASUREMENT rather than by inference - inference being exactly what produced the superseded clause AM-S4S-D7.
SECTION_C_F_AUD_2_DECISIVE_PRE_IMPLEMENT.relationship_to_the_existing_prior_art: The existing full-Supabase harness cannot answer this question as it stands, and never tried to. MEASURED: supabase/migrations/20260716000001_storage_policies.sql defines all three storage.objects policies (select_evidence, insert_evidence, delete_evidence) in terms of bucket_id plus public.can_read_evidence_object(name, auth.uid()) or public.can_write_evidence_object(name, auth.uid()), and contains NO reference to session_id or to request.jwt.claims. The prior art therefore proves the SUBJECT reaches the storage policy path and proves nothing about the SESSION.

Every negative control MUST additionally establish that the intended predicate is what refused - by asserting the SETUP succeeded, by showing the positive twin of the same fixture PERMITS, or by discriminating the SQLSTATE where one is reachable. A negative control that asserts only 'false' is vacuous under the EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS helper shape recorded at F-S4S-1 and does not discharge its obligation.
SECTION_D_PRESERVED_BINDING_REQUIREMENTS.R8_disposable_teardown: The substrate MUST be torn down, and the teardown MUST be VERIFIED rather than assumed.
SECTION_D_PRESERVED_BINDING_REQUIREMENTS.R9_no_developer_global_supabase_state: The gate MUST NOT depend on any developer-global Supabase state - no shared project ref, no shared Docker volume, no already-running stack on the host, and no supabase start against the repository's own supabase/config.toml project_id. A probe that opens one session, sets the claims itself, and calls the helper FABRICATES on one connection exactly the propagation production lacks. Every control that claims to prove a transport property must use the real transport or at minimum two distinct connections. A single-session harness silently passes a fabricated propagation. SECTION_F_POSITIVE_TWIN_AND_404_NON_VACU.status: FROZEN. A strengthening of v1.0.0 SECTION_7 RULE_2 for the specific observable the Storage API produces.
SECTION_F_POSITIVE_TWIN_AND_404_NON_VACU.rule: ANY negative Storage read or download assertion that observes a 404 or an 'Object not found' response MUST have a SUCCESSFUL POSITIVE TWIN in the SAME run, on the SAME stack, against the SAME bucket, through the SAME endpoint shape. A negative read without such a twin is VACUOUS and does not discharge its control.
SECTION_F_POSITIVE_TWIN_AND_404_NON_VACU.what_it_prevents: The Storage API returns 'Object not found' for an unauthorized read rather than a distinguishable authorization error. That single observable is therefore produced identically by: an honest policy denial; a wrong base URL; a wrong bucket name; a wrong or missing path prefix; a bucket that was never created; and a stack that is not yet up. Without a positive twin, any of those five configuration failures masquerades as proof that the selected-organization boundary held - and the gate goes green while proving nothing.
SECTION_F_POSITIVE_TWIN_AND_404_NON_VACU.why_this_is_not_already_covered_by_RULE_: RULE_2 offers THREE alternative discharges - assert the setup succeeded, show a positive twin, or discriminate the SQLSTATE. For a Storage 404 the third is UNAVAILABLE (there is no SQLSTATE on the HTTP path) and the first is INSUFFICIENT (a correct fixture setup says nothing about whether the REQUEST was correctly addressed). For this observable the positive twin is not one option among three; it is the only sufficient one, and this section makes it mandatory rather than elective.
SECTION_F_POSITIVE_TWIN_AND_404_NON_VACU.MEASURED_prior_art_and_why_it_is_not_eno: tests/integration/rls.test.ts already exhibits the shape: 'Analyst A puede subir archivo (INSERT) y leerlo (SELECT)' uploads and downloads successfully and asserts the body text, and the immediately following 'Admin B NO puede leer archivo de Org A (SELECT cruzado fallido)' asserts error.message contains 'Object not found' for the SAME fileName, in the same file, same run, same bucket, same endpoint shape. That is a correct positive twin. But it is INCIDENTAL - a consequence of test ordering, not an enforced property - and nothing in that suite would fail if a future edit removed, reordered, renamed or skipped the positive case. This section converts the incidental into the required, and the companion manifest amendment arms it with a mutation control.
SECTION_F_POSITIVE_TWIN_AND_404_NON_VACU.scope: Applies to every negative Storage read and download in the effective S4s contract, including RI-02 and RI-03 on their read surfaces, and to any successor control that observes a 404 or a not-found message from the Storage API.
SECTION_F_POSITIVE_TWIN_AND_404_NON_VACU.relationship_to_RI_P_05: RI-D-P-05 in the companion manifest amendment is the control that asserts this rule holds over the suite; RI-D-M-02 is the mutation that proves the assertion is armed rather than decorative.

OPEN_FINDINGS.finding: The defect corrected here was produced by a keyword search over SERVICE NAMES in a codebase that reaches those services through an SDK. The search could not have found the capability regardless of its result, and its ZERO result was then treated as a positive measurement of absence.
OPEN_FINDINGS.disposition: Recorded as a transferable lesson rather than a repository defect. A future authority asserting MEASURED ABSENCE of a CAPABILITY must state the search it ran AND justify why that search would have found the capability had it been present. v1.0.0 is preserved unedited specifically so this lesson stays legible.
